 India Voter ID cards, not Aadhaar, to 
access Panchayati Raj benefits now 
 Rajiv Ranjan stated that biometric authentication, along with the voter identification card number or EPIC number, will now be the only valid method for receiving payments and benefits. Image used for representational purposes only. (File Photo) Jitendra Choubey Updated on :  31 Oct 2026, 2:17 am 2 min read 
 Copied 
 NEW DELHI: Union Minister of Panchayati Raj and Fisheries, Rajiv Ranjan, alias Lalan Singh, on Friday announced that a new panchayati raj scheme will render Aadhaar-based payments and benefits outdated. He stated that biometric authentication, along with the voter identification card number or EPIC number, will now be the only valid method for receiving payments and benefits.
 “Aadhaar is currently the basis for payments to beneficiaries, but it will no longer be considered the primary means of identification,” said Singh.
 “Organisations that issue Aadhaar cards are available in every locality.” He further explained, “Going forward, the Aadhaar card will no longer serve as the basis for identifying beneficiaries. Instead, beneficiaries will need to provide biometric authentication along with their EPIC (Voter ID Number). These will serve as their identification credentials, and payments will be made based on that information.”
 Singh was speaking at a day-long national workshop on the People’s Plan Campaign (PPC) for 2026-27, where he announced the new panchayat scheme in the national capital.
 Recently, a prime minister-led Cabinet Committee approved a centrally sponsored scheme named the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana (PM VGSY), which replaces the existing Rashtriya Gram Swarajya Abhiyan. This new scheme aligns with Viksit Bharat 2047 and is set for implementation from 2026-27 to 2030-31, co-terminus with the Sixteenth Finance Commission period.
 Singh urged officials to work on integrating Drinking Water and sanitation, rural development, and Panchayati Raj schemes within the new scheme and to create a digital infrastructure. “Under the new scheme, the converged plan should be prepared based on needs rather than demand,” Singh emphasised. He also encouraged panchayats to generate their own funds to complement the allocations from the 16th Finance Commission.
 “Twenty per cent of the Finance Commission funds for panchayats will be tied to their performance. This means panchayats should aim to increase their own revenue from local resources,” Singh stated.
 Additionally, he highlighted a study conducted by IIM-Ahmedabad, which developed a module on how to increase funds from one’s own sources of revenue. Singh hailed PM Narendra Modi for consistently increasing the funds for the panchayats. Even the 16th Finance Commission allocated `4.35 lakh crore, he said. He also exhorted panchayats to generate their own funds to complement the current allocation.
 “But this amount is not enough for the panchayats, but we have to increase our own source of revenue,” said Singh.
 Move after Cabinet approves new scheme 
 Recently, a prime minister-led Cabinet Committee approved a centrally sponsored scheme named the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana (PM VGSY), which replaces the existing Rashtriya Gram Swarajya Abhiyan. This new scheme aligns with Viksit Bharat 2047.
